The investigated samples were GaN thin layers with embedded ferromagnetic γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N nanocrystals, fabricated by metal organic vapor phase epitaxy.
The nanocrystals had a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure with the (100) planes parallel to the [0001] c-growth direction of the wurtzite GaN matrix.
The lattice parameter of the nanocrystals along the c-growth direction increased with decreasing normalized Ga flow during growth.
The DAFS analysis showed that Ga preferentially occupied the 3c Wyckoff sites in the fcc γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N structure, rather than the 1a sites.
The amount of Ga in the 3c sites, as determined from the DAFS analysis, ranged from 0.10 to 0.31 across the sample series.
The magnetic moment and Curie temperature (T_C) of the nanocrystals decreased with increasing Ga content in the 3c sites, in contrast to the case of Ga occupying the 1a sites.
The T_C of the nanocrystals ranged from 450K to 500K, well above room temperature, for Ga contents up to 30% in the 3c sites.
The nanocrystal density increased from 3.9 x 10^9 NC/cm^2 to 15.0 x 10^9 NC/cm^2 as the normalized Ga flow during growth was increased.
The combination of AXD and DAFS allowed the researchers to distinguish between Ga atoms in the GaN matrix and those incorporated into the embedded nanocrystals.

The DAFS analysis revealed that the local structure of the nanocrystals was slightly distorted from the ideal fcc Pm-3m crystal structure, with the Ga-Fe and Ga-Ga distances deviating from the expected values.
The magnetic response of the GaδFeN layers consisted of a paramagnetic Brillouin-like contribution from Fe^3+ ions in the matrix and a ferromagnetic contribution from the embedded nanocrystals.
The amount of Fe^3+ ions substituting for Ga in the matrix was estimated to be 0.1 ± 0.02%, well below the solubility limit of 0.4%.
The normalized magnetization of the nanocrystals was obtained by dividing the magnetic moment by the diffracted intensity, which is proportional to the nanocrystal volume fraction.
The normalized magnetization and T_C of the nanocrystals showed an inverse correlation with the amount of Ga in the 3c sites.

The results demonstrate the potential of the combined AXD and DAFS approach for unraveling the local structure of similar magnetic phase-separated systems, even when the nanocrystals and the surrounding matrix contain the same absorber element.
